addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

Excludes Omarchy source development in ~/.local/share/omarchy/ and `omarchy dev` workflows.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". aiTitle: Investigate LLM context depth performance regression

content.text: I'll start by pulling up what's already known about this.

content.content:
---
name: context-depth-rates
description: "Prefill and decode rates against cache depth after P7, the two costs P7 removed, and the ~115k-cell ceiling where the timestamp pathology still kills the run."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fd0fc64c-0b09-499f-a092-c4a9c28c6222
  modified: 2026-09-21T13:02:38.935Z
---

**P7, 2026-09-21** closed the depth regression that the 2026-09-19 sweep
recorded. Write-up: `research/p7-context-depth.md`; CSVs
`results/p7_depth_{before,after}[_run2].csv`.

Two passes of each arm, same hour, 48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 512
-tg 64`, ctx 66,880, corpus `wiki.test.raw` (means):

| depth | pp before | pp after | tg before | tg after |
|------:|----------:|---------:|----------:|---------:|
| 0 | 616.9 | 692.7 | 27.96 | 33.18 |
| 8,000 | 530.2 | 583.7 | 15.75 | 22.94 |
| 16,000 | 495.5 | 559.4 | 11.12 | 20.58 |
| 32,000 | 416.5 | 534.5 | 6.78 | 18.34 |
| 64,000 | 313.1 | 441.2 | 4.05 | **16.27** |

Decode falloff to 64k **0.14x → 0.49x**; prefill **0.51x → 0.64x**. `-gen`
at ctx 32768 is **32.43 → 35.92 tok/s**.

**The two costs, because both are easy to reintroduce.**

1. **`nKV` is the allocated cache, not the context.** Three kernels looped on
   it: `llm_attn_score.comp` over `nKV/ratio` pooled blocks,
   `llm_attn_select.comp` over `nKV` cells in four radix passes and an emit.
   That was **6.94 ns an allocated cell a token an attention layer**, paid in
   full *at depth zero* — 10.9 ms of a decode step at 131k cells. It is why
   the old sweep started at 24.27 tok/s where the headline decode is 36.19:
   **a depth-0 number is only comparable at the same `-ctx`.**
2. **QSA was a mask and never a skip.** `llm_attn_wmma.comp` walked every key
   block at every depth. Now a key block with nothing selected in it is
   skipped whole (bit-identical — it already contributed nothing).

**The gate to run after touching any of this**:
`go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer`. Everything
else in `gpu_qsa4k_test.go` has `nKV` equal to the live cell count and cannot
see this regime at all — see [[two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate]]. Above it,
`cmd/llm -gen -n 48 -temp 0 -ctx 32768` on two binaries must give the same 48
tokens.

**Still open**: the **gather** (compact the ≤2051 selected cells' K and V and
run a 2051-cell attention — flat in depth by construction; it is the
remaining 1948 ms of a 64k decode step's 3665), and **128,000 still does not
complete** — the fill dies at ~115k with

    shim: 43 of 1025 timestamp slots never became ready (first 982, last 1024)

the P0 pathology reached by depth instead of row count. Raising the deadline
is not the fix (`vk/shim.c:690`); the untried route is making
`DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional.

**How to apply:** quote the P7 table, not the old one; never compare two
depth-0 rates measured at different `-ctx`. Needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

## The five verticals, at a glance

All five of `GOALS.md`'s models run end to end in Go on Vulkan, validated
against a reference, and are served by `cmd/serve`. The competition from
here is our own ceiling, not a reference implementation.

| vertical | model | headline, measured | open |
|---|---|---|---|
| text generation | qwen3.8-flash-next (180 B, 6 B active) | decode **36.19 tok/s, 1.44x** llama.cpp at **+1.74%** perplexity; prefill **1213.5 tok/s at 8192 rows, 3.10x**, still climbing where llama.cpp plateaus; **16.27 tok/s at 64k of context, 4.02x P7's baseline** | batching (P6); the QSA gather; 128k; speculation parked at 0.95x |
| speech → text | parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 | an 11 s clip in **43 ms — 257x real time**, whole model resident | S10 front end (48% of the pipeline); S9 long clips |
| text → speech | Kokoro-82M | **31 ms for 3.25 s (105x)**, **162 ms for 19.5 s (120x)** — flat per second of audio; the endpoint answers in 59 ms | the vocoder's 20 ms of arithmetic; three small boundaries |
| image generation + editing | Qwen-Image-2.1 | 1024², 40 steps in **1m28.8s**, 31.5 GB resident, native RGBA; streaming previews cost **0.3%**; the fp32 oracle's picture to mean **3.4e-4**. **Edits answer too**: **1m54.2s** on one reference at 1024², 39.4 GB, the oracle's edit to max abs **0.0014** | **parked 2026-09-21** — Q0–Q12 all closed; the 1184²-area ceiling is the one capability left unbuilt |
| embeddings | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | a text in **11.5 ms**, the card's similarity matrix to 1.3e-4 over HTTP | E7 batching, worth up to 10x on short texts |

**The server** (`API.md`): one process, one flag per vertical, OpenAI-shaped
(`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/audio/*`,
`/v1/images/*`, `/v1/embeddings`), plus a Wyoming door for Home Assistant
(`-wyoming`, byte-identical audio to the HTTP door). Everything unimplemented
is refused with a reason, never faked.

**Deployment is two machines**: the language model alone on one (~84 GB
resident), the other four verticals on the other (image ~32 GB, the rest
~3 GB together). `-llm` and `-image` do not fit in one 128 GB process, on
purpose — so no footprint quantisation is planned for the small verticals.

**Where the work goes next.** With the image vertical parked, nothing in the
repo is mid-stage: every open item below is a fresh start, and each vertical's
list is in its own rough order of value. The context-depth regression that
stood at the head of this list was **P7**, closed 2026-09-21: decode at 64k
is **4.05 → 16.27 tok/s (4.02x)** and the falloff from depth zero **6.9x →
2.0x**, from three kernels that walked the *cache* rather than the *context*
plus a QSA selection that was a mask and never a skip
([`research/p7-context-depth.md`](research/p7-context-depth.md)). What is
left of it is the **gather** — the only route to a decode rate that does not
care how long the conversation is — and **128k still not completing**. After
that the two capability gaps are P6 batching (blocked on a product question:
will the API serve more than one stream?) and E7's batched embeddings, worth
up to 10x on short texts; the largest single-vertical percent is S10, the
speech front end at 48% of its pipeline.

---

## Text generation (archive: [`research/llm-vertical.md`](research/llm-vertical.md), review: [`research/llm-review.md`](research/llm-review.md))

**Where it stands.** Phases 1 and 2 are done on both axes and every P-stage
through P5 is closed. The shipped configuration is **D19 + D20 + D21**
(4.5-bit dense bank with a fifth bit on three families, the MoE rows
transcoded, `ffn_down_exps` at IQ4_NL): 4.132 GB a token against a 58.6
tok/s ceiling, perplexity 4.0992 (+1.74% of our own 4.0289, which is itself
−0.13% against llama.cpp's at identical weights). Decode 36.19 tok/s,
prefill 1089 tok/s at ubatch 2048. Served with prefix reuse; a second turn
extends the graph's state rather than re-prefilling.

**Speculation (P5) is built, lossless, and parked at 0.95x.** The rollback
costs nothing when off. What would take it past 1.0, in order: the draft

# P7 — context depth: the cache's size was not the context's depth

> Measured 2026-09-21 on this machine, both arms the same hour, the shipped
> banks (D19 + D20 + D21). The baseline arm is the binary built from the
> commit this work started on; every number below is an interleaved A/B of
> the two binaries, never a comparison against a stored CSV.

## The finding

Decode fell **6.9x between depth 0 and 64 000 cells** (27.90 → 4.04 tok/s)
and prefill halved, and TODO.md recorded it as the vertical's largest
measured regression with the attribution open: *"all of it is attention"*,
with the note that the 2051-cell read cap says the selection is not the term
that grows.

It was two terms, not one, and neither was the selection.

**1. Three kernels walked the cache and not the context.** `nKV` is the
cell count the arenas were *allocated* for — 131 072 in a served process —
and `llm_attn_score.comp` scored all `nKV/ratio` pooled blocks, while
`llm_attn_select.comp` ran four radix passes and an emit over all `nKV`
cells. Neither number has anything to do with how deep the conversation is.
The cost is therefore paid **at depth zero, in full**, and it is linear in
the cache:

| cells allocated | 2048 | 4096 | 8192 | 16384 | 32768 | 65536 | 131072 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| attention, ms / 32 decode tokens, one layer, **empty cache** | 12.9 | 14.5 | 15.3 | 17.1 | 20.7 | 28.2 | **42.7** |

That is **6.94 ns per allocated cell, per token, per attention layer** —
**10.9 ms of a decode step** across the twelve attention layers at 131 072
cells, before a single cell is real. It is most of why the recorded sweep
starts at 24.27 tok/s where the headline decode is 36.19: the sweep
allocates a 131 456-cell cache and the headline does not.

**2. QSA was semantics and not a saving.** `llm_attn_wmma.comp` read the
selection bitmask exactly where it read the causal mask — out of the block
row max and out of P — and so walked **every** key block at every depth,
just as `build_attn_qsa` does. A decode step names 2051 cells however deep
the cache is; it was reading 64 000 of them. Measured slope: **0.25 µs per
live cell, per token, per attention layer** — 192 ms of a 248 ms token at
64k, which is the 85.6% attention share the sweep reported.

L4b-3 had written this down and left it: *"QSA becomes an optimisation at
decode, and only there… skipping unselected key blocks is the whole point.
L7's."* It was never L7's.

## The fix, and why it is bit-identical

Three changes, all of them *identities* rather than approximations, which is
what let the whole thing be gated on exact equality.

**The dead pooled blocks share one score.** `llm_attn_idx.comp` pools cell 0
`ratio` times for every block past the last whole one, and leaves the
position at 0 so the row is unrotated — so all `nBlocks - nBid` of them hold
*the same 128 halves* and therefore the same score. The kernel now computes
that one dot product and broadcasts it, instead of computing it tens of
thousands of times. **The tensor it writes is unchanged**, which is why
`TestAttnGPUIndexer`'s reference comparison still holds row for row.

**The selection is cut against the live cells.** Every cell past
`SEQ_PAST + T` is an `-inf` the causal mask wrote, and `-inf` is the
smallest key `f2ui` has: it can never be picked, so the four radix passes
and the emit skip it. The row *stride* stays `nKV`'s — the arenas are still
cut against the cache — and the row's remaining bitmask words are zeroed
rather than left stale, so `Selection()` still reads as a bitmask over the
whole cache. `desired` is clamped to the live count, since below the width
the selection is the identity and a `desired` the row cannot reach would
leave the bucket search with nothing to find. A useful side effect: at
shallow depth the row now fits `SEL_LDS` and the radix passes come out of
LDS instead of DRAM.

**A key block with nothing selected in it is skipped whole.** The bitmask is
staged *before* the block is read rather than after, and if no row has a bit
in it the iteration is skipped. This is exactly the existing masking, moved
earlier: an unselected cell already contributed nothing to O and nothing to
the row sum, so a block of them contributed nothing, and `blkMax` staying
`-inf` already had its `mo == mn` guard. One consequence had to be handled —
a pad row used to stage all-ones so its softmax denominator would not be
zero, which would have defeated the skip on every decode step (fifteen pad
rows of sixteen). It now stages zero and the epilogue turns a zero
denominator into a zero row, which is strictly better than the garbage it
wrote before, in an arena nothing reads either way.

## The gate

`TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` is new and it is the one that
matters: the 4k fixture staged twice, once in its own 4096-cell cache and
once in a cache three times too big, demanding **identical bits** out of
`attn_gated-3` and `attn_output-3` and the identical selected-cell set on
all 4096 rows. Every other test in `gpu_qsa4k_test.go` runs with `nKV`
equal to the live cell count, so nothing distinguished "the cache is this
big" from "the context is this deep" — which is the whole of what changed.
It passes, and so does the rest of `./llm`.

This is the shape P5c-6 and the two-row regime warn about: a block test that
cannot see the regime is not a gate on it.

And the graph gate above the block gate, for the same reason: `cmd/llm -gen
-n 48 -temp 0 -ctx 32768` on both binaries returns the **same 48 tokens**,
token for token, on a 131k-capable build in a cache 4 700 times the prompt.

## What it bought

**48 layers, the shipped banks, one sequence walked forwards, `-pp 512
-tg 64`, corpus `wiki.test.raw`.** Both arms in the same hour, the cache cut
at the sweep's own requirement (66 880 cells), **two passes of each arm** —
this is also the reproducibility pair TODO.md said the depth figures still
owed. Means below; the within-arm spread is ≤0.5% at every depth on the new
arm and ≤0.6% on the old except at 8 000, where the old arm moved 5%.

| depth | pp before | pp after | | tg before | tg after | |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 616.9 | **692.7** | 1.12x | 27.96 | **33.18** | 1.19x |
| 8 000 | 530.2 | **583.7** | 1.10x | 15.75 | **22.94** | 1.46x |
| 16 000 | 495.5 | **559.4** | 1.13x | 11.12 | **20.58** | 1.85x |
| 32 000 | 416.5 | **534.5** | 1.28x | 6.78 | **18.34** | 2.71x |
| 64 000 | 313.1 | **441.2** | 1.41x | 4.05 | **16.27** | **4.02x** |

Per-arm, tok/s, pass 1 / pass 2 — `tg` before **27.90 / 28.01**, **15.35 /
16.14**, **10.99 / 11.25**, **6.72 / 6.83**, **4.04 / 4.06**; after
**33.18 / 33.18**, **23.13 / 22.75**, **20.49 / 20.66**, **18.35 / 18.32**,
**16.32 / 16.22**.

**The regression itself**, which is the falloff and not the level:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| prefill, depth 0 → 64 000 | 0.51x | **0.64x** |
| decode, depth 0 → 64 000 | **0.14x** (6.9x down) | **0.49x** (2.0x down) |
| attention share of a 64k decode step | 85.6% | 49.7% |
| attention, ms / 64 tokens at 64k | 13 581.8 | **1 948.0** (7.0x) |

And the level, not the falloff, moves too, because the cache-walk was
charged at every depth: `cmd/llm -gen -n 48 -temp 0 -ctx 32768` is
**32.43 → 35.92 tok/s**, which is 1.29x llama.cpp to **1.43x** and 85% of
the byte ceiling to **94%**.

The 4-layer probe says where each half of it came from, ms of attention per
32 decode tokens in a 131 072-cell cache, two interleaved passes:

| depth | 0 | 4 096 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 42.5 / 42.5 | 74.4 / 74.3 | 175.9 / 175.3 | 580.4 / 585.5 |
| after | 14.8 / 14.9 | 43.7 / 43.9 | 75.5 / 75.5 | **87.5 / 87.5** |

The depth-zero column is the cache-walk; the 65 536 column is the skip. The
skip does **better than the estimate** — ~513 selected blocks over 2 000 key
blocks predicts four in five empty, and the curve is flatter than that,
because the selection is clustered rather than uniform.

## What is still open

**Decode is still O(depth), just with a much smaller constant.** The skip
prunes key blocks; it does not make the cost independent of how many there
are to prune. The constant-cost version is the **gather** L4b declined:
compact the ≤2051 selected cells' K and V into a contiguous scratch and run
a 2051-cell attention, which is flat in depth by construction. That is the
remaining 1 948 ms of the 64k decode step above, and it is the only route to
a rate that does not care how long the conversation is.

**Prefill's falloff is not this bug.** At ubatch 512 and ~50% density a
32-cell key block is eight indexer blocks and the chance all eight miss is
~0.4% (L4b-3), so the skip is close to inert there; what prefill gained
(1.11-1.40x) is the cache-walk, and the 0.64x that remains is the quadratic
term any dense attention has. llama.cpp has the same one.

**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it: the fill
dies at ~115k cells in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth instead of
row count. The untried route is unchanged — make `DispatchMultiMarked`'s
per-dispatch marks optional, since they are pure instrumentation and
wall-clock tok/s would survive losing the per-block breakdown at that depth.

**The cell expansion is the last O(nKV) loop.** `llm_attn_score.comp` still
writes `-inf` into every cell of the row past the live count, because that
tensor is compared against `indexer_score_tokens-3` in full and the mask has
to agree exactly. It is 6.3 MB of stores a token across the twelve layers,
~0.1% of a step, and it is written down rather than done.

This is the shape P5c-6 and the two-row regime warn about: a block test that
cannot see the regime is not a gate on it.

And the graph gate above the block gate, for the same reason: `cmd/llm -gen
-n 48 -temp 0 -ctx 32768` on both binaries returns the **same 48 tokens**,
token for token, on a 131k-capable build in a cache 4 700 times the prompt.

## What it bought

**48 layers, the shipped banks, one sequence walked forwards, `-pp 512
-tg 64`, corpus `wiki.test.raw`.** Both arms in the same hour, the cache cut
at the sweep's own requirement (66 880 cells), **two passes of each arm** —
this is also the reproducibility pair TODO.md said the depth figures still
owed. Means below; the within-arm spread is ≤0.5% at every depth on the new
arm and ≤0.6% on the old except at 8 000, where the old arm moved 5%.

| depth | pp before | pp after | | tg before | tg after | |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 616.9 | **692.7** | 1.12x | 27.96 | **33.18** | 1.19x |
| 8 000 | 530.2 | **583.7** | 1.10x | 15.75 | **22.94** | 1.46x |
| 16 000 | 495.5 | **559.4** | 1.13x | 11.12 | **20.58** | 1.85x |
| 32 000 | 416.5 | **534.5** | 1.28x | 6.78 | **18.34** | 2.71x |
| 64 000 | 313.1 | **441.2** | 1.41x | 4.05 | **16.27** | **4.02x** |

Per-arm, tok/s, pass 1 / pass 2 — `tg` before **27.90 / 28.01**, **15.35 /
16.14**, **10.99 / 11.25**, **6.72 / 6.83**, **4.04 / 4.06**; after
**33.18 / 33.18**, **23.13 / 22.75**, **20.49 / 20.66**, **18.35 / 18.32**,
**16.32 / 16.22**.

**The regression itself**, which is the falloff and not the level:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| prefill, depth 0 → 64 000 | 0.51x | **0.64x** |
| decode, depth 0 → 64 000 | **0.14x** (6.9x down) | **0.49x** (2.0x down) |
| attention share of a 64k decode step | 85.6% | 49.7% |
| attention, ms / 64 tokens at 64k | 13 581.8 | **1 948.0** (7.0x) |

And the level, not the falloff, moves too, because the cache-walk was
charged at every depth: `cmd/llm -gen -n 48 -temp 0 -ctx 32768` is
**32.43 → 35.92 tok/s**, which is 1.29x llama.cpp to **1.43x** and 85% of
the byte ceiling to **94%**.

The 4-layer probe says where each half of it came from, ms of attention per
32 decode tokens in a 131 072-cell cache, two interleaved passes:

| depth | 0 | 4 096 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 42.5 / 42.5 | 74.4 / 74.3 | 175.9 / 175.3 | 580.4 / 585.5 |
| after | 14.8 / 14.9 | 43.7 / 43.9 | 75.5 / 75.5 | **87.5 / 87.5** |

The depth-zero column is the cache-walk; the 65 536 column is the skip. The
skip does **better than the estimate** — ~513 selected blocks over 2 000 key
blocks predicts four in five empty, and the curve is flatter than that,
because the selection is clustered rather than uniform.

## What is still open

**Decode is still O(depth), just with a much smaller constant.** The skip
prunes key blocks; it does not make the cost independent of how many there
are to prune. The constant-cost version is the **gather** L4b declined:
compact the ≤2051 selected cells' K and V into a contiguous scratch and run
a 2051-cell attention, which is flat in depth by construction. That is the
remaining 1 948 ms of the 64k decode step above, and it is the only route to
a rate that does not care how long the conversation is.

**Prefill's falloff is not this bug.** At ubatch 512 and ~50% density a
32-cell key block is eight indexer blocks and the chance all eight miss is
~0.4% (L4b-3), so the skip is close to inert there; what prefill gained
(1.11-1.40x) is the cache-walk, and the 0.64x that remains is the quadratic
term any dense attention has. llama.cpp has the same one.

**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it: the fill
dies at ~115k cells in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth instead of
row count. The untried route is unchanged — make `DispatchMultiMarked`'s
per-dispatch marks optional, since they are pure instrumentation and
wall-clock tok/s would survive losing the per-block breakdown at that depth.

**The cell expansion is the last O(nKV) loop.** `llm_attn_score.comp` still
writes `-inf` into every cell of the row past the live count, because that
tensor is compared against `indexer_score_tokens-3` in full and the mask has
to agree exactly. It is 6.3 MB of stores a token across the twelve layers,
~0.1% of a step, and it is written down rather than done.

---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
---
name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks

---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].

content.text:
Let me give you a status update while that finishes.

**What I found.** P7 (committed this morning) already took 64k decode from 4.05 → 16.27 tok/s. What was left was attributed as "the gather". That attribution turns out to be wrong, and I have the measurement to show it.

I added per-kernel resolution to the depth bench — and found a bug in the instrument while doing it: `GraphStats.Kinds` is a map, so every snapshot aliased the live graph and each depth's row was polluted by the *next* depth's fill. Only the last depth in any sweep was ever trustworthy. Fixed with `GraphStats.Clone()`.

With clean numbers, the decode falloff at 64k (one attention layer, ms/token) is:

| kernel | depth 0 | 65536 | growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attn.attn` | 0.142 | 1.975 | **1.832 (70%)** |
| `attn.score` | 0.041 | 0.303 | 0.262 |
| `attn.select` | 0.009 | 0.174 | 0.165 |

Then the decisive probe: I cut the attention grid from 24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work and a twelfth of the traffic — and it measured **1.00x at every depth**. So the cost is neither bandwidth nor head redundancy. The 24 head-workgroups are single waves that all fit on 40 CUs at once, so the dispatch's wall clock is *one wave's serial walk over key blocks*, and nothing about the other 23 changes it. A gather would help, but only incidentally — the actual lever is cutting the walk.

content.text: Let me write up the finding while the sweep runs.

input.command:
cat > research/p8-decode-attention-split.md <<'MDEOF'
# P8 — the decode attention was one wave's walk, not the cache's size

> Measured 2026-09-21 on this machine, interleaved A/B of the same binary
> under `LLM_ATTN_SPLITS=1` (the unsplit control) and the default, two passes
> of each arm in the same hour. It follows P7
> (`research/p7-context-depth.md`) and is the second half of the same
> question.

## What P7 left, and why its attribution was wrong

P7 closed the depth regression the 2026-09-19 sweep recorded — decode at 64k
from 4.05 to 16.27 tok/s — and named what was left as **the gather**: compact
the ≤2051 selected cells' K and V into a contiguous scratch and run a
2051-cell attention, "the only route to a rate that does not care how long the
conversation is". That was the remaining 1 948 ms of a 64k decode step.

The premise under it was that the kernel's cost is the *cells it reads*. It is
not, and one probe says so.

**Cutting the attention grid from 24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work
and a twelfth of the traffic — measured 1.00x at every depth.**

| depth | 0 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attn.attn`, 24 workgroups (ms/token, one layer) | 0.142 | 1.930 | 1.975 |
| the same with the grid cut to `NHeadKV` | 0.142 | 1.927 | 1.976 |

The grid is (query blocks, heads). At decode that is (1, 24): **24 workgroups,
each a single wave**, and this device has 40 compute units, so all of them run
at once and the dispatch's wall clock is one wave's serial walk over the key
blocks. Twelve of those waves share each of the two KV planes and re-read it
in full, which looks like the obvious waste and is not the cost — removing it
removes nothing, because the twelve were never queued behind each other.
Neither is the QSA selection's scatter, and neither is bandwidth: with one
wave per CU there is nothing to hide a `coopMatLoad`'s latency behind.

So the lever is not what the walk reads. It is **how long the walk is**, and
the gather is only one way to shorten it — by making the cells fewer. Cutting
the axis across more workgroups shortens it without touching the cells at all,
works at every depth rather than only past the width, and needs no second
layout for K and V.

## The finding, in one line

A decode step's attention is latency-bound on a single wave, and the model has
**24 waves of work where the device wants hundreds**.

## What changed

**`llm_attn_wmma.comp` gains a `-DSPLITK` build.** The key axis is cut
`splits` ways, the grid's x carries (query block, slice), and each slice runs
its own online softmax over its own blocks and writes the result
**unnormalised** — beside the two numbers that let it be resumed, its row max
and its row sum. `llm_attn_combine.comp` folds the slices together, and does
the softmax divide and the output gate that the unsplit epilogue does. That is
flash-decoding's split.

**The slices are strided, not contiguous, and that is a correctness
requirement.** L7a's gate is that a prompt run in pieces equals the prompt run
whole, bit for bit. The natural cut — `[0, last)` into `splits` runs — fails
it, because `last` is `min(n, past + q0 + BM)` and both `n` and `q0` belong to
the *batch*: a seven-token chunk and a one-token chunk put the boundaries in
different places and fold the partial softmaxes in a different order. A stride
is immune — block b is slice `b % splits` however the run was cut — and the
blocks past a row's causal extent that the stride then walks cost nothing and
change nothing, for exactly the reason the unsplit loop can walk them: blkMax
stays -inf, the correction is exactly 1.0, and P is zeroed. The stride also
balances the slices where a contiguous cut would not, because P7's selection
is clustered.

**The slice count is a constant, and every other candidate is a bug.** It must
not move with `SEQ_PAST`, because a decode step's command buffer is recorded
once and replayed byte for byte (P1c). And it must not be read off `nKV` —
the tempting one, since a deep arena is where the split pays — because
`TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` gates that the cache's *size*
changes nothing about the answer, and a slice count read off `nKV` would
change the order the partial softmaxes fold and so the last places of the
result. That is P7's own class of bug, re-entered through the rounding rather
than through the cost. So the number is fixed at 16 and the slices' *contents*
are the live depth.

## It is not bit-identical, and the repo already had a place for that

It cannot be: the rescales happen in a different order and fp32 addition is
not associative. `PinSchedule` is where this vertical puts such kernels —
L7d's split-K GEMV, L8d's three MoE rungs, L8e's two projections — and the
split attention is the sixth. The equalities are asserted with the pin on; the
"one token at a time, on the decode schedule" subtest is what measures the
cost of taking it off, and its bar is unchanged at 1e-3 rms.

What the split adds there, measured:

| | result_norm rms against the one-shot prefill |
|---|---|
| decode schedule, split off | 6.626e-04 |
| decode schedule, split on | **7.067e-04** |

And at the layer's own output, where the comparison is against llama.cpp
rather than against the other kernel — which is the comparison that decides
whether it is *wrong*, since neither kernel is the truth:

| | rms against llama.cpp, one decode step at cell 4095 |
|---|---|
| unsplit | 9.211e-04 |
| 16 slices | **9.213e-04** |

The two are indistinguishable. Between the arms themselves the difference is
1.26e-04 rms, and it is **flat in the slice count** — 1.02e-04 at two slices,
1.26e-04 at sixteen — which is the signature of the fp16 `P` rounding under a
different max sequence rather than of accumulated reassociation. The selection
is identical, cell for cell, on all 2051.

## What it bought

**The 4-layer prefix (one attention layer), two passes of each arm,
interleaved, `-ctx 131072 -pp 512 -tg 32`.** Means:

| depth | 0 | 4 096 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attention block, split off (ms/token) | 0.463 | 1.365 | 2.356 | 2.734 |
| attention block, split on | **0.355** | **0.489** | **0.708** | **1.050** |
| | 1.30x | 2.79x | 3.33x | **2.60x** |

The flash kernel alone, which is what was cut:

| depth | 0 | 4 096 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attn.attn`, unsplit | 0.142 | 1.021 | 1.927 | 1.978 |
| `attn.attn.split` + `attn.attn.combine` | 0.035 | 0.143 | 0.276 | **0.295** |
| | 4.1x | 7.1x | 7.0x | **6.7x** |

The combine is flat at 0.006 ms — one dispatch a layer, 24 workgroups of four
waves over a 393 KB arena — and it is the whole of what the split costs.

**It pays at depth zero too**, 1.30x, which the gather could not have: at a
few hundred cells there is nothing to compact, but there are still only 24
waves, and sixteen slices of one block each is 384.

## What is still open

**`attn.score` is now the largest kernel in the block at depth**, and it is
the same structural bug: `llm_attn_score.comp` is dispatched one workgroup a
token, so a decode step scores every pooled block of the context on **one**
compute unit of forty. `llm_attn_select.comp` is the same shape. After the
split, at 65 536 cells and one attention layer:

| kernel | ms/token | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `attn.score` | 0.304 | one workgroup, `nBid` block dots + an `nKV` cell expansion |
| `attn.attn.split` | 0.289 | the split flash attention |
| `attn.qkv` | 0.182 | flat in depth |
| `attn.select` | 0.176 | one workgroup, four radix passes over the live cells |

Together `score` and `select` are 0.480 ms of the block's 1.050 at 64k, and
both are **bit-identically** parallelisable — unlike the attention, neither
sums anything across the split, so cutting them costs no reassociation at all.
The score's one dependency is that its cell expansion reads every block's
score, which makes it two dispatches rather than one.

**The gather is still available and is now worth less.** It would cut
`attn.attn.split`'s 0.289 ms, not the 1.978 P7 costed it against.

**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it.
MDEOF
echo written; wc -l research/p8-decode-attention-split.md

content.text: Let me stop polling and update the write-up for P9 while the suite finishes.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='research/p8-decode-attention-split.md'
s=open(p).read()
old = """## What is still open

**`attn.score` is now the largest kernel in the block at depth**, and it is
the same structural bug: `llm_attn_score.comp` is dispatched one workgroup a
token, so a decode step scores every pooled block of the context on **one**
compute unit of forty. `llm_attn_select.comp` is the same shape. After the
split, at 65 536 cells and one attention layer:

| kernel | ms/token | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `attn.score` | 0.304 | one workgroup, `nBid` block dots + an `nKV` cell expansion |
| `attn.attn.split` | 0.289 | the split flash attention |
| `attn.qkv` | 0.182 | flat in depth |
| `attn.select` | 0.176 | one workgroup, four radix passes over the live cells |

Together `score` and `select` are 0.480 ms of the block's 1.050 at 64k, and
both are **bit-identically** parallelisable — unlike the attention, neither
sums anything across the split, so cutting them costs no reassociation at all.
The score's one dependency is that its cell expansion reads every block's
score, which makes it two dispatches rather than one.
"""
new = """# P9 — the indexer was on one compute unit of forty

Splitting the attention left `attn.score` as the **largest kernel in the
block at depth**, and it is the same structural bug one dispatch over:
`llm_attn_score.comp` was dispatched one workgroup a token, so a decode step
— one token — scored every pooled block of the context, and then wrote every
cell of a 131 072-cell row, on a single compute unit. After P8, at 65 536
cells and one attention layer:

| kernel | ms/token | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `attn.score` | 0.304 | one workgroup: `nBid` block dots **and** an `nKV` cell expansion |
| `attn.attn.split` | 0.289 | the split flash attention |
| `attn.qkv` | 0.182 | flat in depth |
| `attn.select` | 0.176 | one workgroup, four radix passes over the live cells |

**What pinned it was a barrier.** The expansion reads `score[t][blk]` for an
arbitrary block, so every block had to be scored before any cell was
expanded, and inside one workgroup that is a `barrier()` — which is exactly
what stopped the scoring from being spread over more than one workgroup. Two
dispatches with a pipeline barrier between them is the same ordering with the
workgroup count let go of. So the expansion moved to
`llm_attn_expand.comp`, and both halves are striped over the grid's y.

**It is bit-identical, and that is the gate.** Neither kernel sums anything
across the stripe — every output element is one read, one add and one store —
so which lane writes it is not observable.
`TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` demands the score, the expanded
cells and the selection back **to the last bit** at 2, 7, 16 and 64 stripes,
and gets them. That is a stronger gate than a tolerance on the layer's output
would be, and deliberately: a dropped cell score is one -inf among 2051
selected cells, which moves the answer by almost nothing and moves the
*selection* by a cell. `PinSchedule` has no business with this one.

## What is still open

**`attn.select` is the last of the three**, and it is the hard one:

content.text:
I've chained the sweep to start as soon as the test suite finishes. Second finding while that runs:

**P9 — the QSA indexer was on one compute unit of forty.** After the attention split, `attn.score` became the block's largest kernel at depth. Same structural bug: it was dispatched one workgroup per token, so a decode step scored every pooled block of the context *and* wrote every cell of a 131,072-cell row on a single CU. What pinned it was a `barrier()` — the cell expansion reads every block's score, and inside one workgroup that ordering *is* a barrier. Splitting it into two dispatches (`score` + a new `llm_attn_expand.comp`) keeps the ordering and lets the workgroup count go.

That one is **bit-identical** — neither kernel sums across the stripe, so which lane writes an element isn't observable. `TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` demands the score, the expanded cells and the selection back to the last bit at 2, 7, 16 and 64 stripes, and gets them.

content.text:
Both changes are in and gated; I'm waiting on the definitive 48-layer numbers. Summary of where this landed:

**The regression was misattributed, and the probe that showed it is the main result.** P7 left "the gather" as the remaining work — compact the ≤2051 selected cells so attention reads fewer of them. But cutting the attention grid from 24 workgroups to 2 (a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic) measured **1.00x at every depth**. The 24 head-workgroups are single waves that all fit on 40 CUs simultaneously, so the dispatch's wall clock is one wave's serial walk over key blocks. The cells it reads were never the lever; the *length of the walk* is.

**Two changes, both landed:**

- **P8** splits the key axis across workgroups (flash-decoding) with a combine pass. The flash kernel at 64k goes **1.978 → 0.295 ms** (6.7x), the attention block **2.734 → 1.050** (2.6x). Not bit-identical — it reassociates — so it joins the five kernels `PinSchedule` already covers; it moves `result_norm` from 6.63e-4 to 7.07e-4 rms on a 1e-3 bar, and against llama.cpp the two arms are 9.211e-4 vs 9.213e-4, indistinguishable.
- **P9** unpins the QSA indexer, which was scoring the whole context on one CU of forty because a `barrier()` held the score and its cell expansion in one dispatch. Bit-identical at every stripe count.

Two things worth flagging that I found on the way and did not cause:

1. **The depth bench's per-label attribution was silently wrong** — `GraphStats.Kinds` is a map, so every snapshot aliased the live graph and each depth's row absorbed the *next* depth's fill. Only the last depth of any sweep was ever trustworthy. Fixed via `Clone()`.
2. **Decoding one token at a time from cell zero does not match a batched prefill**, pre-existing and unrelated to my change: the pooled indexer's `nBid` depends on where the *batch* ends, so a token whose tail block is incomplete in one schedule and complete in another gets a different score, and the selection is discontinuous. It doesn't arise in served use (prefill batches are wide), but it means `even(nTok, 1)` is not a valid reference schedule for an equality test.

cat > /home/kube/.claude/projects/-home-kube-repos-strix-halo-vulkan/memory/decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth.md <<'EOF'
---
name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
places).

The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.

So at decode:

- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
  concurrently.
- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
  nothing.)
- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.

Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.

**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.
EOF

cat > /home/kube/.claude/projects/-home-kube-repos-strix-halo-vulkan/memory/never-edit-source-during-a-sweep.md <<'EOF'
---
name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
a crash.

**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.
EOF

---
name: graphstats-kinds-aliases
description: "`st := g.Stats` shares the Kinds map with the live graph, so a kept snapshot keeps absorbing later dispatches; take GraphStats.Clone() instead."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**2026-09-21.** `llm.GraphStats` is all scalars except `Kinds
map[string]DispatchStat`. So `st := g.Stats` copies the timings by value and
**shares the per-label map by reference**: the scalar columns freeze, the
label rows do not, and a caller that keeps several snapshots ends up with
per-label times that include work belonging to a later measurement while the
block columns beside them disagree.

It bit the depth sweep, which keeps one snapshot a depth a phase. The fills
between depths run *after* `ResetStats` for the previous depth's `tg`, so
depth 0's label row absorbed the 4 096-fill, depth 4 096's absorbed the
16 384-fill, and depth 16 384's absorbed the 65 536-fill — 96 batches of 512
tokens landing in a row divided by 32 decode tokens. It read as
`attn.attn` at **70.6 ms a token** against a 9.9 ms step, and the tell was
`n_per_pass` coming back 1.2 / 1.7 / 4.0 / 1.0 for a kernel that runs once a
pass. **Only the last depth of any sweep was ever trustworthy.**

`GraphStats.Clone()` now exists and `cmd/llm/bench_depth.go` uses it. The
scalar-only readers (`reportPhases`, `bench_graph.go:152`,
`generate.go:129`) were never affected.

**How to apply:** never keep `g.Stats` across another pass — call `.Clone()`.
And when a per-label number is absurd, check `n_per_pass` against how many
times that kernel actually runs in a pass before believing the milliseconds;
it is the column that exposes contamination.
EOF

TODO.md:58:([`research/p7-context-depth.md`](research/p7-context-depth.md)). What is
TODO.md:100:  2026-09-21** ([write-up](research/p7-context-depth.md)). It was two terms
research/README.md:106:| [P7](p7-context-depth.md) | **Context depth was the cache's size, not the context's depth: decode at 64k 4.05 → 16.27 tok/s (4.02x), the falloff from depth zero 6.9x → 2.0x, and the level moves too (`-gen` at ctx 32768 32.43 → 35.92, 94% of the byte ceiling).** Two terms and neither was the selection's width. **Three kernels walked `nKV`** — the cells the arenas were *allocated* for — instead of the cells that exist: `llm_attn_score.comp` scored all `nKV/ratio` pooled blocks and `llm_attn_select.comp` ran four radix passes and an emit over all `nKV` cells, which is **6.94 ns an allocated cell a token an attention layer** and is charged *at depth zero, in full* — **10.9 ms of a decode step** at 131k cells before a single cell is real, and most of why the recorded sweep began at 24.27 tok/s where the headline decode is 36.19. **And QSA was semantics and not a saving**: `llm_attn_wmma.comp` read the bitmask exactly where it read the causal mask, so it walked **every** key block at every depth just as `build_attn_qsa` does — a decode step names 2051 cells however deep the cache is and it was reading 64 000 of them, **0.25 µs a live cell a token a layer**, which is the 85.6% attention share at 64k. L4b-3 had written the skip down and left it to L7; it was never L7's. The fix is three **identities**, which is what let the whole thing be gated on exact equality: the dead pooled blocks all hold cell 0 pooled `ratio` times and unrotated, so `nBlocks - nBid` dot products are **one**; a cell past `SEQ_PAST + T` is an `-inf` and `-inf` is the smallest key `f2ui` has, so the radix never looks at it (and the row now fits `SEL_LDS` at shallow depth); and a key block with nothing selected in it already contributed nothing to O and nothing to the row sum, so it is **skipped whole**. One consequence had to be handled — a pad row staged all-ones for its softmax denominator and would have defeated the skip on fifteen rows of sixteen at every decode step. **The gate is the new `TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer`**: the 4k fixture staged in its own cache and in one three times too big, identical bits out of `attn_gated-3` and `attn_output-3` and the identical selected-cell set on all 4096 rows — because every other test in `gpu_qsa4k_test.go` has `nKV` equal to the live cell count and so cannot tell "the cache is this big" from "the context is this deep". Above it, 48 greedy tokens identical token for token across the two binaries. Two interleaved passes of each arm, ≤0.5% within-arm spread. **What is left is the gather** — compacting the ≤2051 selected cells' K and V, which is flat in depth by construction — and **128k, which still does not complete** |

content.text:
I've been polling too aggressively. The sweep needs ~30 more minutes of wall clock; I'll let the armed notifications deliver it rather than checking every few seconds.

Here's where the work stands, with everything that's already measured and gated:

**Root cause (the part I'm confident in, and it's the reusable finding).** P7 attributed the remaining depth cost to the cells attention reads, and proposed the gather. That attribution is wrong. Cutting the attention grid from 24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic — moved the dispatch **1.00x at every depth**. The 24 head-workgroups are single waves that all fit on 40 CUs at once, so the dispatch costs one wave's serial walk over key blocks. Nothing about traffic or head-redundancy is on the critical path; only the length of that walk is.

**P8 — split the key axis** (`-DSPLITK` + `llm_attn_combine.comp`). Slices are *strided*, not contiguous, because `last` depends on the batch and a contiguous cut would break L7a's chunk-equality. The count is a fixed constant: deriving it from `nKV` would have re-entered P7's own bug class through the rounding. Measured on the 4-layer probe, two passes per arm:

| | depth 0 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 65,536 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flash kernel, unsplit | 0.142 | 1.021 | 1.927 | 1.978 |
| split + combine | 0.035 | 0.143 | 0.276 | **0.295** |
| | 4.1x | 7.1x | 7.0x | **6.7x** |

**P9 — unpin the QSA indexer.** It was scoring the whole context on one CU of forty, held there by a `barrier()` between the score and its cell expansion. Split into two dispatches, both striped. Bit-identical at 2/7/16/64 stripes.

**Correctness.** Full `./llm` suite green. P8 reassociates, so it joins the five kernels `PinSchedule` already covers — it moves `result_norm` 6.63e-4 → 7.07e-4 rms on a 1e-3 bar, and against llama.cpp the arms are 9.211e-4 vs 9.213e-4.

**48-layer confirmation, in flight.** The base arm has already reproduced P7's published table (33.20 / 23.20 / 20.56 / 18.48 / **16.15** tok/s), which validates the protocol; the P8 and P8+P9 arms are running.

import csv
S="/tmp/claude-1000/-home-kube-repos-strix-halo-vulkan/9096da0b-120b-44a1-bb43-2c038b45a6c6/scratchpad"
depths=[0,8000,16000,32000,64000]
def load(arm,p):
    d={}
    for r in csv.DictReader(open(f"{S}/q_{arm}_{p}.csv")):
        d[(r["phase"],int(r["depth"]))]=(float(r["tok_s"]), float(r["attn_ms"]), float(r["ms_per_token"]))
    return d
A={(a,p):load(a,p) for a in ("base","p8","p89") for p in (1,2)}
def mean(a,ph,d,i): return (A[(a,1)][(ph,d)][i]+A[(a,2)][(ph,d)][i])/2
print("=== decode, tok/s (mean of two passes; pass1/pass2) ===")
print(f"{'depth':>7} | {'base':>18} | {'+P8':>18} | {'+P8+P9':>18} |{'x':>7}")
for d in depths:
    row=f"{d:>7} |"
    for a in ("base","p8","p89"):
        row+=f" {A[(a,1)][('tg',d)][0]:8.2f}/{A[(a,2)][('tg',d)][0]:<8.2f}|"
    row+=f"{mean('p89','tg',d,0)/mean('base','tg',d,0):>6.2f}x"
    print(row)
print()
print("=== decode falloff, depth 0 -> 64000 ===")
for a,n in (("base","P7 baseline"),("p8","+P8"),("p89","+P8+P9")):
    print(f"  {n:<14} {mean(a,'tg',64000,0)/mean(a,'tg',0,0):.2f}x   ({mean(a,'tg',0,0):.2f} -> {mean(a,'tg',64000,0):.2f} tok/s)")
print()
print("=== attention block, ms/token (12 layers) ===")
print(f"{'depth':>7} |{'base':>9} |{'+P8':>9} |{'+P8+P9':>9} |{'x':>7}")
for d in depths:
    b,e,f=mean('base','tg',d,1),mean('p8','tg',d,1),mean('p89','tg',d,1)
    print(f"{d:>7} |{b:>9.2f} |{e:>9.2f} |{f:>9.2f} |{b/f:>6.2f}x")
print()
print("=== step, ms/token ===")
for d in (0,64000):
    print(f"  depth {d:>6}: {mean('base','tg',d,2):.1f} -> {mean('p89','tg',d,2):.1f} ms")
print()
print("=== prefill, tok/s (unchanged by design: split is decode-only) ===")
for d in depths:
    print(f"  {d:>6}: base {mean('base','pp',d,0):7.1f}   p89 {mean('p89','pp',d,0):7.1f}")

**48 layers, the shipped banks (D19 + D20 + D21), P7's protocol exactly — one
sequence walked forwards, `-pp 512 -tg 64`, ctx 66 880, corpus
`wiki.test.raw` — three arms interleaved, two passes of each, one binary

within-arm spread, which is what makes the rest of this comparable to it.
CSVs: `results/p8_depth_{base,split}[_run2].csv`,
`results/p9_depth_after[_run2].csv`.

Decode, tok/s, means of two passes:

| depth | base (P7) | +P8 | +P8+P9 | |
|------:|----------:|----:|-------:|---|
| 0 | 33.20 | 34.77 | **35.06** | 1.06x |
| 8 000 | 23.30 | 31.50 | **32.10** | 1.38x |
| 16 000 | 20.56 | 30.24 | **31.11** | 1.51x |
| 32 000 | 18.46 | 28.15 | **29.24** | 1.58x |

25.11**, +P8+P9 **27.04 / 27.12**. The within-arm spread is ≤1.8% at every

**The regression itself**, which is the falloff and not the level:

| | before P7 | P7 | P8 | P9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode, depth 0 → 64 000 | 0.14x | 0.49x | 0.72x | **0.77x** |
| decode at 64 000, tok/s | 4.05 | 16.30 | 24.92 | **27.08** |
| a decode step at 64 000 | — | 61.4 ms | — | **36.9 ms** |

The attention block itself, ms a token across the twelve layers:

| depth | 0 | 8 000 | 16 000 | 32 000 | 64 000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 4.57 | 16.44 | 20.62 | 25.75 | 30.46 |
| +P8 | 3.20 | 5.31 | 6.39 | 8.21 | 11.12 |
| +P8+P9 | **3.02** | **4.77** | **5.51** | **6.64** | **8.13** |
| | 1.51x | 3.45x | 3.74x | 3.88x | **3.74x** |

531.4 → 534.8, 438.8 → 441.9 tok/s across the five depths — inside the noise

was done on — three seconds to stage against ninety — and it is here because

The twelve query heads that share each KV plane and re-read it in full are free to delete and worth nothing; with one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a `coopMatLoad` behind, which is why the kernel achieved ~7 GB/s where prefill on the same code achieves hundreds. **P8** is flash-decoding's split: `-DSPLITK` cuts the key axis 16 ways, each slice runs its own online softmax and writes an **unnormalised** partial beside its row max and row sum, and `llm_attn_combine.comp` folds them and does the divide and the gate. The slices are **strided and not contiguous**, which is a correctness requirement and not a preference — `last` is `min(n, past + q0 + BM)` and both terms are the *batch's*, so contiguous cuts put the boundaries in different places for a seven-token chunk than for a one-token one and break L7a's chunk equality; block b belongs to slice `b % splits` however the run was cut. The count is a **constant**: off `SEQ_PAST` it would stale P1c's prerecorded decode step, and off `nKV` it would make the cache's size change the last places of the answer, which is P7's own class of bug re-entered through the rounding. It is not bit-identical and cannot be, so it joins the five kernels `PinSchedule` already covers (L7d's GEMV, L8d's three, L8e's two) — it moves `result_norm` 6.626e-04 → 7.067e-04 rms on a 1e-3 bar, and against **llama.cpp** the two arms are 9.211e-04 and 9.213e-04, indistinguishable; the split-vs-unsplit difference is 1.26e-04 rms and **flat in the slice count** (1.02e-04 at two), which is fp16 `P` rounding under a different max sequence and not accumulated reassociation. **P9** is the same finding one dispatch over: `llm_attn_score.comp` was one workgroup a token, scoring every pooled block *and* writing every cell of a 131 072-cell row on one CU of forty, pinned there by the `barrier()` its cell expansion needed. name: context-depth-rates
description: "Prefill and decode rates against context depth after P7/P8/P9, what each removed, and the gates to run after touching attention; 128k still dies on the timestamp pathology."

**The depth regression is closed, in three stages, all 2026-09-21.** Decode at
64 000 cells went **4.05 → 16.30 → 24.92 → 27.08 tok/s** and the falloff from
depth zero **0.14x → 0.49x → 0.72x → 0.77x**. Write-ups:
`research/p7-context-depth.md`, `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`. CSVs
`results/p7_depth_*`, `results/p8_depth_*`, `results/p9_depth_after*`.

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 512 -tg 64`, ctx 66 880, `wiki.test.raw`,
three arms interleaved, two passes each (means):

| depth | base (P7) | +P8 | +P8+P9 | pp |
|------:|----------:|----:|-------:|---:|
| 0 | 33.20 | 34.77 | **35.06** | 690 |
| 8 000 | 23.30 | 31.50 | **32.10** | 578 |
| 16 000 | 20.56 | 30.24 | **31.11** | 556 |
| 32 000 | 18.46 | 28.15 | **29.24** | 535 |
| 64 000 | 16.30 | 24.92 | **27.08** | 442 |

A decode step at 64k: **61.4 → 36.9 ms**. The attention block across twelve
layers: **30.46 → 8.13 ms** a token (3.74x).

**What each stage removed.**

1. **P7 — `nKV` is the allocated cache, not the context.** Three kernels
   looped on it, paid in full *at depth zero*; and QSA was a mask and never a
   skip. See its own write-up — both are easy to reintroduce.
2. **P8/P9 — at decode the kernels are single waves that all fit at once.**
   See [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]]; this is the reusable one. P8
   splits the attention's key axis 16 ways (strided, constant count, folded
   by `llm_attn_combine.comp`); P9 splits the indexer's score from its cell
   expansion so both can stripe.

**Prefill is untouched by P8/P9 and that is the control** — 692.6 → 690.5 at
depth 0 and 438.8 → 441.9 at 64 000, inside the noise. Prefill's 0.63x
falloff is the quadratic term any dense attention has; llama.cpp has it too.

**The gates after touching any of this**:

    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P7
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSplitMatchesUnsplit               # P8
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer  # P9, exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph

`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS=1` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=1` are the control arms.
**P8 is not bit-identical** and is covered by `PinSchedule` with the other
five reassociating decode kernels; P9 **is** bit-identical.

token (0.176 ms a token a layer at 64k) and is a reduction, so it needs a
two-level histogram rather than a stripe. **128 000 still does not complete**
— the fill dies at ~115k in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth; the
untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional.
The gather P7 named is still available and now worth much less.

compare two depth-0 rates measured at different `-ctx`. Needs
`LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].
