content.text:
Done. The context-depth regression is closed.

## Result

**64k decode: 16.30 → 27.08 tok/s (1.66x). A decode step at 64k: 61.4 → 36.9 ms. Falloff from depth zero: 0.49x → 0.77x.** Against the pre-P7 baseline of 4.05 tok/s, that's 6.7x.

| depth | base (P7) | +P8 | +P8+P9 | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 33.20 | 34.77 | 35.06 | 1.06x |
| 8,000 | 23.30 | 31.50 | 32.10 | 1.38x |
| 16,000 | 20.56 | 30.24 | 31.11 | 1.51x |
| 32,000 | 18.46 | 28.15 | 29.24 | 1.58x |
| 64,000 | 16.30 | 24.92 | **27.08** | **1.66x** |

Attention across the twelve layers: 30.46 → 8.13 ms/token at 64k. Prefill is untouched (438.8 → 441.9 at 64k) — that's the control, since the split is decode-only.

## What it actually was

P7 left "the gather" as the remaining work, on the premise that the cost is the cells attention reads. **That premise was wrong.** Cutting the attention grid from 24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic — measured **1.00x at every depth**. The grid is (query blocks, heads); a decode step is one token; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes every workgroup a single wave; the device has 40 CUs. All 24 run at once, nothing queues, and the dispatch costs **one wave's serial walk**. The twelve query heads re-reading each KV plane are free to delete and worth nothing.

So: **P8** splits the key axis 16 ways (strided — contiguous cuts break chunk-equality because `last` depends on the batch; and the count is constant because deriving it from `nKV` would re-enter P7's own bug class through the rounding). **P9** unpins the indexer, which was scoring the whole context on one CU of forty, held there by a `barrier()`.

## Correctness

Full suite green. P8 reassociates, so it joins the five decode kernels `PinSchedule` already covers: `result_norm` 6.626e-4 → 7.067e-4 rms on a 1e-3 bar, and against llama.cpp the two arms are **9.211e-4 vs 9.213e-4** — indistinguishable. The split-vs-unsplit difference is flat in slice count (1.02e-4 at two, 1.26e-4 at sixteen), which is fp16 `P` rounding, not accumulated error. P9 is bit-identical at 2/7/16/64 stripes.

## Two things I found that you didn't ask about

1. **The depth bench's per-label attribution was silently wrong.** `GraphStats.Kinds` is a map, so snapshots aliased the live graph and each depth absorbed the *next* depth's fill — `attn.attn` read 70.6 ms/token against a 9.9 ms step. Only the last depth of any sweep was ever trustworthy. Fixed with `Clone()`; the tell is `n_per_pass` not matching how often a kernel runs.
2. **Decoding one token at a time from cell zero doesn't match a batched prefill** — pre-existing, not mine. The pooled indexer's `nBid` depends on where the *batch* ends, so a token whose tail block is incomplete in one schedule and complete in another scores differently, and the selection is discontinuous. Invisible in served use (prefill batches are wide), but it means `even(nTok, 1)` isn't a valid reference for an equality test.

I also lost ~25 minutes of measurement by editing source while a `go run`-per-arm sweep was live; the script now builds once. That, the decode-latency finding, and the stats trap are saved to memory.

**Still open:** `llm_attn_select.comp` is the last kernel on one workgroup per token (0.176 ms/token/layer at 64k) — it's a reduction, so it needs a two-level histogram rather than a stripe. And 128k still doesn't complete.

p='research/p8-decode-attention-split.md'
s=open(p).read()
old = """## What is still open

**`attn.select` is the last of the three**, and it is the hard one:
`llm_attn_select.comp`'s four radix passes are a reduction over the row, so
cutting it across workgroups needs a two-level histogram rather than a
stripe. It is 0.176 ms a token a layer at 64k.

**The gather is still available and is now worth much less.** It would cut
`attn.attn.split`'s 0.289 ms, not the 1.978 P7 costed it against.
"""
new = """# P10 — the selection could not be split, so it was widened

`attn.select` was the last of the three and the only one that **cannot** be
spread over the grid. Its four radix passes are a *reduction* over the row:
each pass narrows a threshold by eight bits using a histogram of everything
that matched the bits already fixed, so pass n+1 cannot start until pass n has
finished everywhere. Striping it the way P9 stripes the score would need a
global barrier between every pass — two dispatches each, nine a layer,
~96 extra dispatches a decode step at twelve layers, which at the ~6 µs a
dispatch the combine costs is more than the kernel spends.

**So the parallelism it got is waves, not workgroups.** At 65 536 cells the
row is 64 000 uints and `SEL_LDS` holds 4 096, so every one of the five passes
— four radix and the emit — streams the row out of DRAM again: 1.28 MB, from
one workgroup, on one compute unit. The workgroup was 256 lanes, four wave64s,
and four waves have nothing to hide a DRAM round trip behind. The width was
tied to the radix size by the bucket search, which is one lane per bucket; it
is now a build knob, and the shipped rung is **1024 lanes, sixteen waves**.

Two things had to be true for that to be free. The bucket search is a suffix
sum over `histo[tid]`, so lanes past the radix carry a zero count — and they
have to be held out of the `atomicMax` that elects the bucket, because a pass
whose `desired` has fallen to zero would otherwise elect the highest *lane*
and put a bucket index that does not exist into `prefix`. The emit's running
`taken` is already computed identically on every lane through a wave scan and
`shWave[WG/64]`, so it widens without change.

**It is bit-identical, and that is the gate**:
`TestAttnGPUSelectWidthDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` runs a 4095-token prefill and
a decode step at both widths and demands the selected set **and** the layer's
output back to the last bit. It gets them, on 8 400 896 selected cells.

| depth | 0 | 16 384 | 65 536 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attn.select`, 256 lanes (ms/token, one layer) | 0.0069 | 0.0491 | 0.1744 |
| `attn.select`, 1024 lanes | 0.0080 | **0.0287** | **0.0932** |
| | 0.86x | 1.72x | **1.87x** |

Depth zero pays 0.0011 ms for the wider launch over a row that fits LDS
anyway, which is the shape of the trade and is 0.01% of a step.

## What is still open

**The gather, and it is now the only large one left.** After P8, P9 and P10,
what a decode step still gains between depth 0 and 64 000 is 5.9 ms a token,
and `attn.attn.split` is 3.0 of it — the split shortened the walk sixteenfold
but did not stop it being a walk over every key block. The gather P7 named is
the way to make it a walk over 2 051 cells instead, and it is worth what that
3.0 ms is, not the 1.978 ms a layer P7 costed it against.

**More slices is not the answer, and that is measured.** At 65 536 cells
`attn.attn.split` runs 0.318 / 0.288 / 0.291 / 0.283 ms a token at 8 / 16 / 32
/ 64 slices while the combine behind it climbs 0.004 / 0.006 / 0.010 / 0.018.
Sixteen is a plateau: past it the walk stops getting shorter and only the fold
gets longer.

**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it.
"""
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
old2 = """**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it.
"""
# remove the now-duplicated trailing line (the original one at the very end)
if s.count("**128 000 still does not complete**") > 1:
    i = s.rindex("**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it.")
    # keep the one inside the new block (which is earlier), drop a trailing dup
    tail = s[i:]
    if tail.strip() == "**128 000 still does not complete**, and nothing here touches it.":
        s = s[:i].rstrip() + "\n"
open(p,'w').write(s)
print(s.count("**128 000 still does not complete**"))

aiTitle: Investigate LLM context depth performance regression

content.text:
Status while the 48-layer confirmation runs (~35 min, three arms × two passes):

**P10 is done and gated.** The selection is the one kernel that genuinely *cannot* be split across workgroups — its four radix passes are a reduction, so pass n+1 can't start until pass n finishes everywhere, and a global barrier between each would cost ~96 extra dispatches per decode step at twelve layers. So the parallelism it got is **waves, not workgroups**: 256 lanes → 1024, sixteen wave64s instead of four on the one CU it lands on, which is what hides the five DRAM streams it makes of the row at depth.

It's **1.87x at 64k** (0.174 → 0.093 ms/token/layer) and bit-identical — `TestAttnGPUSelectWidthDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` checks the selected set *and* the layer output at both widths over a prefill plus a decode step, on 8.4M selected cells.

One thing that needed care: the bucket search is one lane per radix bucket, so lanes past 256 have no bucket. They had to be held out of the `atomicMax` vote — otherwise a pass whose `desired` fell to zero would elect the highest *lane* rather than the highest bucket and put a nonexistent bucket index into `prefix`.

I also swept the P8 slice count and found **16 is already a plateau** — past it the walk stops shortening while the combine grows, so there's no free win there. That's now recorded in the code comment so nobody re-runs it.

Also cleaned up two operational messes of my own making: an orphaned test binary from a `head`-truncated pipeline that was contending for 6.4 GB and the GPU, and a duplicate sweep launch (the chain I thought hadn't fired had in fact fired). Both caught before they corrupted a measurement.

`wiki.test.raw` — three arms interleaved, two passes of each, one binary built

Decode, tok/s, means of two passes:

| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | |
|------:|----------:|-------:|-----------:|---|
| 0 | 33.16 | 35.06 | **35.08** | 1.06x |
| 8 000 | 22.74 | 32.18 | **32.40** | 1.42x |

| 32 000 | 18.06 | 29.14 | **29.68** | 1.64x |
| 64 000 | 15.91 | 26.76 | **27.69** | **1.74x** |

26.71**, +P8+P9+P10 **27.71 / 27.66**. The within-arm spread is ≤2.4% at
every depth and ≤0.2% on the final arm.

**The regression itself**, which is the falloff and not the level:

| | before P7 | P7 | P8+P9 | P10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode, depth 0 → 64 000 | 0.14x | 0.48x | 0.76x | **0.79x** |
| decode at 64 000, tok/s | 4.05 | 15.91 | 26.76 | **27.69** |
| a decode step at 64 000 | — | 62.9 ms | — | **36.1 ms** |

The attention block itself, ms a token across the twelve layers:

| depth | 0 | 8 000 | 16 000 | 32 000 | 64 000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 4.58 | 16.61 | 20.58 | 25.87 | 30.80 |
| +P8+P9 | 3.01 | 4.76 | 5.51 | 6.63 | 8.13 |
| +P8+P9+P10 | **3.03** | **4.63** | **5.30** | **6.21** | **7.28** |
| | 1.51x | 3.58x | 3.88x | 4.17x | **4.23x** |

**Prefill is untouched, which is the control.** All three changes are decode
paths and nothing else: prefill reads 691.1 → 691.3, 579.8 → 579.1, 557.6 →
558.8, 532.6 → 531.8, 440.7 → 439.6 tok/s across the five depths — inside the
noise at every one. Prefill's 0.64x falloff is the quadratic term any dense
attention has and is not this bug; llama.cpp has the same one.

"""

content.text:
Done. Full suite green on an uncached run, machine idle.

## Where the depth regression ended up

| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 33.16 | 35.06 | 35.08 | 1.06x |
| 8,000 | 22.74 | 32.18 | 32.40 | 1.42x |
| 16,000 | 20.53 | 31.12 | 31.35 | 1.53x |
| 32,000 | 18.06 | 29.14 | 29.68 | 1.64x |
| 64,000 | **15.91** | 26.76 | **27.69** | **1.74x** |

**A decode step at 64k: 62.9 → 36.1 ms. Falloff from depth zero: 0.48x → 0.79x.** Attention across twelve layers: 30.80 → 7.28 ms/token (4.23x). Against the pre-P7 baseline of 4.05 tok/s, 64k decode is now **6.8x**. Prefill unchanged at every depth — the control holds, since all three changes are decode-only.

## What this session added on resume

**P10.** The selection is the one kernel that *can't* be split — four radix passes are a reduction, so pass n+1 waits on pass n everywhere, and a global barrier between each is ~96 extra dispatches per step at twelve layers, more than the kernel costs. So it got waves instead of workgroups: 256 lanes → 1024, sixteen wave64s on the one CU it lands on, which is what hides the five DRAM streams it makes of the row. **1.87x at 64k, bit-identical** — the gate checks the selected set *and* the layer output at both widths over a prefill plus a decode step.

The subtle part: lanes past the radix have no bucket, and had to be held out of the `atomicMax` vote. Without that, a pass whose `desired` fell to zero would elect the highest *lane* rather than the highest *bucket* and put a nonexistent bucket index into the threshold.

**A negative result worth having:** I swept the P8 slice count and 16 is already a plateau — 0.318 / 0.288 / 0.291 / 0.283 ms at 8/16/32/64 while the combine climbs 0.004 → 0.018. No free win there; it's recorded in the code so nobody re-runs it.

## What's left

**The gather is now the only large item.** Of the 5.9 ms a decode step still gains between depth 0 and 64k, the split attention is 3.0 of it — P8 shortened the walk sixteenfold without stopping it being a walk over *every* key block. The gather makes it a walk over 2,051 cells instead. And 128k still doesn't complete.

Two operational messes I caused and caught: an orphaned test binary from a `head`-truncated pipeline contending for the GPU, and a duplicate sweep launch (the chain I thought hadn't fired had). Both killed before they polluted a measurement — the final sweep is a single clean three-arm, two-pass run.
